entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the said complaint, offence got registered against the petitioner and in pursuance thereof, the police during the course of investigation sealed the factory premises of the petitioner.

Counsel for the petitioner submits that investigation is over; charge-sheet has been filed and in fact,
the petitioner has also been granted the benefit of anticipatory bail by this Court.

He further submits that though an application for releasing the factory premises of the present petitioner has been moved under Section 457 of Cr.P.C. before the Court below, but the same has been rejected vide order dated 22.03.2022 (Annexure A/2) saying that investigation is going on and still there is relevant material and evidence available in the factory and if it is handed over to the petitioner, then it is every likelihood that evidence can be destroyed and manipulated.
Thereafter, a revision was preferred which was also rejected vide order dated 25.03.2022 (Annexure A/1) by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Patan, District Jabalpur.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Patan, District Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved, this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed.
Counsel for the petitioner undertakes that petitioner Firm in future shall not manufacture the duplicate pipes of any other Firm.

Shri Ajay Shukla, learned counsel appearing for the respondent/State opposes the submissions made by counsel for the petitioner and submitted that the impugned orders passed by the Courts below do not call for any interference.

Shri Sankalp Kochar, learned counsel for the intervener also vehementally opposes the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner and submits that if the factory premises is released or handed over to the petitioner, then there is every possibility that the petitioner again start production of duplicate pipes in the name and style of the interevener and at this stage, it would not be proper to release the factory.
He submits that under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petition deserves to be dismissed.

He further submits that whatever articles seized by the police,
those are the subject matter of the case and lying in the police station and if the same are released then the petitioner will sell the those articles in the market which will cause damage to the intervenor Firm.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and the undertaking given by counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner will not manufacture duplicate pipes in future, I am allowing this petition to the extent that the lock of the factory premises shall be opened and the same be handed over to the petitioner so that she may proceed with the production.
However, the seized articles which are lying in the police station shall not be released till the trial is concluded or without the permission of the Court below.
With the aforesaid, the petition stands allowed and disposed of.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE rao Smt. Maya Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5144133/
